scenarios.user_message: Find Python or AI roles in Hamburg from the last two weeks, no temp agencies.
scenarios.final_message:
I found 11 recent Python / AI listings in Hamburg (last 14 days). I examined six that looked most relevant and assessed fit for up to 8. Shortlist (3–8 listings) with fit summary:

1) NTT DATA — Senior AI Engineer (ref ...307475...) — remote up to 100%
   - Fit: strong on Python, ML frameworks (PyTorch/TensorFlow), MLOps, Generative AI; role covers end-to-end model development and production deployment.
   - Notes: customer-facing/consulting flavor; German (verhandlungssicher) + English required.
2) NTT DATA — Senior AI & GenAI Architect (ref ...305633...) — remote up to 100%
   - Fit: senior architect role focusing on GenAI solutions and technical ownership; similar benefits and remote flexibility.
3) engineering people GmbH — Data Analyst und AI Experte (ref 12727-UL1384214-S)
   - Fit: mentions Python and AI/LLM; salary indicated (€50k–€60k). Less emphasis on production ML engineering — more analyst / supply-chain context.
4) SIGNAL IDUNA — Public Cloud Engineer, Schwerpunkt Generative AI (ref 10001-1003964360-S)
   - Fit: cloud/platform role with Python microservices, Google Cloud, Vertex AI, LangChain, Terraform — good match if you want platform/infra + GenAI.
5) SIGNAL IDUNA — Data Scientist Generative AI (fixed-term) (ref 10001-1003953451-S)
   - Fit: data-science role building Generative AI on Google Cloud; Python + HF/Transformers expected; fixed-term to 31.12.2027.
6) Deutsches Klima Rechenzentrum (DKRZ) — Research Software Engineer HPC (ref 19392-0068492207-S)
   - Fit: scientific HPC role where Python is used alongside Fortran/C++; more research/HPC-focused than standard ML engineering.

Next steps — pick any of:
- Get full extracted fit rubric and evidence quotes for any of these (I can show the detailed dimension scores and ad quotes).
- Save specific listings to your tracker (saved / apply / reject) — tell me which ref(s) and status; I'll save them.
- Broaden or narrow search (e.g., expand radius, include nearby cities, or include temp agencies).

Which of the options do you want now, or which listings should I add to your tracker?

Good question — thanks for asking. I’ll explain using the assessment dimensions and the evidence extracted from the ad for the engineering people GmbH — Data Analyst und AI Experte (ref 12727-UL1384214-S).

Summary of the computed rubric (from the assessment):
- Skills: not met
- Location / remote: partly
- Seniority: partly
- Language: partly
- Employment type: met

Why it’s only partial (evidence + gaps)

1) Skills — why marked as not met
- Positive evidence (match): the ad explicitly lists “Kenntnisse im Umgang mit Python, AI/LLM and Google Workspace.” That shows basic Python and LLM familiarity.
- Missing / weak evidence (gaps): the role asks for several concrete data-engineering and modelling responsibilities that indicate stronger ML/engineering skills than just “Python knowledge.” Examples from the ad:
  - “Extraktion und Integration strukturierter und unstrukturierter Daten … auf Basis der IT‑Datenmodellierung”
  - “Entwicklung, Test und Implementierung geeigneter Analysemodelle”
  - “Analyse und Verbesserung der Modellgenauigkeit”
  - “Entwicklung, Test und Implementierung …” and “Datenvisualisierungen”
  Those responsibilities imply experience with building production-ready pipelines, feature engineering, model lifecycle work and analytics — more than an occasional Python/LLM user. Because the ad requires multiple substantial data/engineering competencies but only states general Python/AI knowledge (no details about frameworks, deployment, MLOps, scale, etc.), the skills dimension is flagged as not met / gap.

2) Location / remote — partly
- Evidence: job location is Hamburg (match).
- Gap: the ad doesn’t mention remote or % remote flexibility. Because you asked for roles in Hamburg and many others offered explicit remote options, the lack of stated remote arrangement makes this only partly matching your preferred remote evidence.

3) Seniority — partly
- Evidence: the ad asks for “mehrjährige Erfahrung” and lists responsibilities across project management and supply-chain context — that implies some mid-level experience.
- Gap: it’s not explicit about seniority level (e.g., “Senior” title or exact years), so seniority is only a partial match.

4) Language — partly
- Evidence: ad says “sehr gute Englisch- und gute Deutschkenntnisse.”
- Gap: your preference may include required German level or flexibility; here German is required at “good” and English “very good,” so language is partially satisfied but depends on your needs.

5) Employment type — met
- Evidence: the ad lists full-time and a salary range (€50k–€60k), and does not appear to be temp agency — so employment type matches.

What this means for you
- The listing is relevant if you want an analyst role that touches AI/LLM and you’re comfortable with a mix of analytics, supply-chain context and some data engineering.
- It’s less relevant if you expect a hands-on production ML engineering role (MLOps, deployment, heavy model training at scale) because the ad doesn’t show strong evidence of those expectations or required tooling (no explicit mention of PyTorch/TensorFlow, Docker/Kubernetes, cloud infra, or MLOps practices). That’s why the overall skills score is low even though Python/AI is present.

If you want, I can:
- Show the exact ad quotes I used for each dimension.
- Mark this listing as saved / apply / reject in your tracker.
- Filter results to only include roles that explicitly list production ML tooling (PyTorch/TensorFlow, MLOps, Docker/K8s, cloud). Which would you prefer?
